CHROMIUM: go2001: Don't immediately wait for replies to (most) messages. To allow for more parallelism, don't wait for messages to be replied to from the point of where they are queued. Instead, queue them and return immediately. To be able to do this, we need an ability to queue messages and not wait for them to be sent to hardware (while the ring buffer is full), which requires pending message memory to be managed separately. Switch to allocating their buffers dynamically. To make this more optimal, use kmem_cache. Messages are allocated when queued to be send to hardware, and freed after copied to the ring buffer, or on error, if still pending at that point. Given that VM_EMPTY_BUFFER messages are scheduled in the interrupt context, their memory has to be allocated beforehand. Do this by allocating in buf_prepare callback and storing the memory on source go2001_buffer. Not waiting for VM_EMPTY_BUFFER messages introduces an additional complication on resolution change. When receiving a resolution change notification in reply from hardware, we may have additional messages pending already, which will be processed and returned to us from hardware with a request to reprocess them after handling the resolution change. To handle this, move all buffers that hardware requested to be reprocessed to a new resume queue. After the resolution change sequence is finished, move them back in front of the source queue for reprocessing. This also requires us to allocate another message buffer for reprocessing at that time. Finally, waiting for context to be finished now involves waiting for the pending message queue to become empty (i.e. messages are moved to the outgoing message ring buffer), followed by waiting for replies to all these messages to arrive from hardware. CHROMIUM: go2001: Remove periodic intra refresh. Sets initial rate control settings instead of relying on hard-coded settings in firmware. This sets QP min/max thresholds to current libvpx ones and explicitly disables periodic intra and buffer refreshes. Disabling periodic refreshes show a significant SSIM/PSNR increase and fewer bitrate spikes (due to keyframes which are more expensive). They were previously enabled/hard-coded due to a race condition in RTCVideoEncoder where two consecutive frames could have the exact same RTP timestamp if they get queued up, causing one of them to be dropped and the bitstream would not be decodable from now on. cryptohome: redefine |TpmInit::IsTpmReady| Taking |Tpm|'s model into consideration, ignore the readiness flag in |TpmPersistentState| if |tpm_managerd| is in charge of TPM readiness logic. The reason is that, |tpm_managerd| can takes command from any permitted client. |cryptohomed| doesn't set the mentioned flag if the ownership-taking command doesn't come from |cryptohome| itself; in this case, the flag doesn't always provide the correct information. Keeping the flag updated inside |cryptohome| seems to be a more decent design choice at the first glance, but the flag is going to be obsoleted once |tpm_managerd| is in charge of TPM readiness for all TPM versions. UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: Fix YUV buffers color rendering Currently, YUV hardware overlays are converted to RGB using a color space conversion different than BT.601. The result is that colors of e.g. NV12 buffers don't match colors of YUV hardware overlays. In order to fix this, enable YUV2YUV and set appropriate coefficients for formats such as NV12 to be displayed correctly. This commit was tested using modetest, gstreamer and chromeos (hardware accelerated video playback). Before the commit, tests rendering with NV12 format resulted in colors not displayed correctly. Test examples (Tested on RK3399 and RK3288 boards connected to HDMI monitor): $ modetest 39@32:1920x1080@NV12 $ gst-launch-1.0 videotestrc ! video/x-raw,format=NV12 ! kmssink Signed-off-by: Daniele Castagna <dcastagna@chromium.org> [ezequiel: rebase on linux-next and massage commit log] Signed-off-by: Ezequiel Garcia <ezequiel@collabora.com> Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20190108214659.28794-1-ezequiel@collabora.com (cherry picked from commit 1c21aa8f2b687cebfeff9736d60303a14bf32768) BUG=chromium:969898 TEST=Build, boot, see graphics Change-Id: I1a4912def9c6c086bb3c9b31203098931beaa4a2 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Cq-Depend: chromium:1652086 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1652085 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/rockchip: Add reflection properties Add the KMS plane rotation property to the DRM rockchip driver, for SoCs RK3328, RK3368 and RK3399. RK3288 only supports rotation at the display level (i.e. CRTC), but for now we are only interested in plane rotation. This commit only adds support for the value of reflect-y and reflect-x (i.e. mirroring). Note that y-mirroring is not compatible with YUV. UPSTREAM: USB: add usbfs ioctl to retrieve the connection speed The usbfs interface does not provide any way for the user to learn the speed at which a device is connected. The current API includes a USBDEVFS_CONNECTINFO ioctl, but all it provides is the device's address and a one-bit value indicating whether the connection is low speed. That may have sufficed in the era of USB-1.1, but it isn't good enough today. This patch introduces a new ioctl, USBDEVFS_GET_SPEED, which returns a numeric value indicating the speed of the connection: unknown, low, full, high, wireless, super, or super-plus. Similar information (not exactly the same) is available through sysfs, but it seems reasonable to provide the actual value in usbfs. FROMLIST: USB: add usbfs ioctl to retrieve the connection parameters Recently usfbs gained availability to retrieve device speed, but there is sill no way to determine the bus number or list of ports the device is connected to when using usbfs. While this information can be obtained from sysfs, not all environments allow sysfs access. In a jailed environment a program might be simply given an opened file descriptor to usbfs device, and it is really important that all data can be gathered from said file descriptor. This patch introduces a new ioctl, USBDEVFS_CONNINFO_EX, which return extended connection information for the device, including the bus number, address, port list and speed. The API allows kernel to extend amount of data returned by the ioctl and userspace has an option of adjusting the amount of data it is willing to consume. A new capability, USBDEVFS_CAP_CONNINFO_EX, is introduced to help userspace in determining whether the kernel supports this new ioctl. CHROMIUM: i915: intel_dp_aux_backlight: Fix max backlight calculations Max backlight value for the panel was being calculated using byte count i.e. 0xffff if 2 bytes are supported for backlight brightness and 0xff if 1 byte is supported. However, EDP_PWMGEN_BIT_COUNT determines the number of active control bits used for the brightness setting. Thus, even if the panel uses 2 byte setting, it might not use all the control bits. Thus, max backlight should be set based on the value of EDP_PWMGEN_BIT_COUNT instead of assuming 65535 or 255. Additionally, EDP_PWMGEN_BIT_COUNT was being updated based on the VBT frequency which results in a different max backlight value. Thus, setting of EDP_PWMGEN_BIT_COUNT is moved to setup phase instead of enable so that max backlight can be calculated correctly. Only the frequency divider is set during the enable phase using the value of EDP_PWMGEN_BIT_COUNT. Also, no flickers observed on boot-up.
